title: Notes on d-matching polynomials, gcd-matrix permanents, and partition self-divisibility, with Lean 4 formalizations
description: Four notes in combinatorics and number theory, with a methodology note, by Vico Bonfioli, each paired with a Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization. The Lean library builds with no sorry, and every mathematical theorem depends only on Lean's three standard axioms. FINAL RELEASE: this repository is closed and no further work is planned. (1) Roots of d-matching polynomials and the spectrum of the universal cover. Hall-Puder-Sawin place the roots of mu_{d,G} in an interval; we conjectured they lie in the spectrum of the universal cover itself, the matching-polynomial form of their Question 6.3. THAT CONJECTURE IS FALSE. The counterexample is due to Chris Hall, on 41 vertices, and is verified here independently. The two hypotheses proposed to repair it are also false, and are refuted here: minimum degree three on 14 vertices, and 3-connectivity on 23, the spectral certificate being exact and its arithmetic machine-checked. The reason none of them could work is the Divisibility Lemma: a separator of size k met by p identical branches forces A^(p-k) to divide mu_G, where A is the branch's own matching polynomial, so the offending root belongs to the divisor and no hypothesis on the ambient graph can reach it. What stands is the closed form for every graph of first Betti number one and every d, with the roots located exactly in the spectrum of the cover. The biregular case is treated separately and is not resolved; its margin for complete bipartite families is positive but decays at the soft-edge exponent, so the statement is tight and no size-free bound can prove it. (2) The permanent of the gcd matrix a(n)=per[gcd(i,j)] (OEIS A085244), whose arithmetic appears unstudied although the determinant is classical (Smith, 1876): a family of congruences, v2(a(n)) tending to infinity, and (a(n)/n!)^(1/n) tending to infinity unconditionally. The 2-adic deficit is stratified by a class-number ladder of depth exactly three; that result is conditional and concerns the weight-zero grade rather than a(n) itself. (3) Coefficient stability of d-matching polynomials. (4) Integers n with n dividing p(n)-1: a minor note on OEIS A128836, which was already published complete to 10^8, recomputed here only to 10^6; it should be read as a case study in the methodology note and not as a result.
